title: Health & Safety Law: Who Must Do What
whatItIs: The Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 puts general duties on employers, the self-employed and employees. On construction sites it is usually enforced by HSE inspectors.

keyFacts.text: Employers MUST ensure, so far as is reasonably practicable, the health, safety and welfare of all employees.
Employers MUST give the information, instruction, training and supervision needed for safety.
Employees MUST take reasonable care of themselves and others affected by what they do or don't do.
You MUST NOT intentionally or recklessly interfere with or misuse anything provided for safety.
An employer MUST NOT charge employees for anything the law specifically requires it to provide.

visual.caption: Who has which duty under the 1974 Act

items.title: Employer to employees
items.text: Health, safety and welfare of all employees (s. 2).

items.title: Employer to others
items.text: Not put others, like the public, at risk, so far as reasonably practicable (s. 3).

items.title: Safety policy
items.text: Written and brought to employees' notice; not needed under 5 employees (s. 2(3)).

items.title: Employees
items.text: Take reasonable care; co-operate with your employer (s. 7).

items.title: Everyone
items.text: Don't interfere with or misuse safety equipment (s. 8).

items.title: HSE inspectors
items.text: Enter sites, question workers, serve notices.

a.label: Improvement notice
points: Requires improvements by a set date
Suspended while an appeal is heard

b.label: Prohibition notice
points: Stops a process or dangerous equipment: risk of serious injury
Not suspended by an appeal unless the tribunal directs

onTheTest.question: Under the 1974 Act, which of these is a legal duty of every employee?
options: Take reasonable care of themselves and others
onTheTest.why: Section 7: employees must take reasonable care of themselves and others affected by what they do, and co-operate with their employer.

onTheTest.question: A worker removes a guard rail to save time and leaves it off. Which legal duty has he broken?
options: Not to interfere with things provided for safety
onTheTest.why: Section 8: no one may intentionally or recklessly interfere with or misuse anything provided for health, safety or welfare.

traps: Safety isn't only the employer's job: employees have legal duties too.
Paying your own tax doesn't automatically make you self-employed under health and safety law.
A prohibition notice stays in force during an appeal unless the tribunal directs; an improvement notice is suspended.
